pick.topic: Business breakdown: FriendFilter + GroupFilter — FriendFilter and GroupFilter are established Chrome extensions for Facebook friend and gro
pick.angle: Two boring Chrome extensions for managing Facebook friends and groups make about $11K a month from ~390 subscribers

research.what_it_does: Chrome extensions that show which Facebook friends (FriendFilter) or group members (GroupFilter) never engage, so you can remove the inactive ones.
research.who_pays: Facebook creators, marketers, influencers and group admins with big friend lists or groups. The free tier is limited, and the paid tiers raise the removal and scan limits.
research.pricing: friendfilter.com: Free $0 (forever free, 5 removals per day). Growth $29/month (scan up to 5,000 friends, 100 removals per day, daily auto-sync, CSV export). Pro $49/month (up to 3 Facebook profiles, auto friend requests, auto reactions, priority support). The $9 intro offer gives 7 days of full Growth access, then renews at $29/mo. The Chrome Web Store listing also shows Annual $199/year. The site shows an 'Annual billing, save up to 40%' toggle.
growth: Chrome Web Store distribution: the FriendFilter listing shows 10,000 users and a 3.8 rating from 142 ratings (store listing, as indexed). The site claims 'Trusted by 120,000+ users'. The GroupFilter store listing says FriendFilter has '15,000+ active users and 120,000+ installs'.

Founder-written Medium post (FriendFilter team): the founder asked in Facebook Groups how to remove inactive friends. The answers he got were bad, so he had his developers build a Chrome extension. The post says it took about 2 months to build.

SEO content: the site runs many landing and comparison pages, such as 'Best Facebook Friend Remover Extensions in 2026 (Compared)', 'Facebook Group Analytics Tool' and 'Facebook Friend Filter Remover Extension'. The TrustMRR listing says an SEO landing page is a growth lever already built.

Affiliate program: friendfilter.com/affiliate says 'up to 50% lifetime recurring commissions'. The pitch targets parenting, tech safety and wellbeing creators. The TrustMRR listing names Rewardful as the affiliate tool.

Cross-sell: GroupFilter's Chrome Web Store page says it is built by the same team as FriendFilter and has been 'trusted by group admins since 2021'. It has 2,000 users and links to the FriendFilter extension.
Low-friction funnel: free forever plan, a 14-day free trial with no credit card, then a $9 7-day Growth trial. The pricing page and FAQ describe each of these.
founder_story: TrustMRR lists the founder as Jeffery Lebowski (X handle fpslebowski, 1,713 followers) and the business as founded March 2019 in the United States.

A FriendFilter team Medium post, written in the founder's first person, says he is a software developer with a full-time staff of developers. He asked his legal team whether such an extension would violate Facebook's rules, and the post says it came back as fine. The post says development took about 2 months.
The TrustMRR listing describes an asset sale to a buyer's LLC with 30 days of transition support, so the business is being sold. Treat the founder as the seller, not a long-term operator.
lessons: Build the product for a pain you saw people ask about publicly. The founder asked in Facebook Groups how to remove inactive friends, then built an extension to solve it.
Ship a real free tier plus a cheap $9 trial to get people in, then charge $29-$49/month once they see the engagement data (pricing page).
Own one narrow, high-intent search niche (Facebook friend remover, group analytics) with dedicated landing and comparison pages.
Add a lifetime recurring affiliate program (up to 50%) so creators, who are the target users, sell it for you.
Extend a working extension into a sibling product (GroupFilter) and cross-link the two.
criticism: Platform risk: it depends on Facebook and Chrome. The site says 'NOT endorsed by Meta / Facebook'. Meta could change the UI or its rules at any time, and the extension would break.

The TrustMRR listing is a business-for-sale listing. Its description claims $11.3K MRR and about 390 subscribers, while the verified figures are $8,237 MRR and 337 active subscriptions. Use the verified figures only.
The Stripe API key has expired, so the revenue data may be stale (last updated Sep 18, 2026). Profit margin is hidden (shown as XX%), so revenue is not profit.
The Chrome Web Store rating is middling: 3.8 from 142 ratings for FriendFilter and 4.3 from 77 ratings for GroupFilter (store pages, as indexed).
Competitors exist, for example Friender, which has a comparison page pricing from $9/month against FriendFilter's $29/month Growth tier.
The extension automates unfriending on Facebook. It may carry account-limit risk, and the support FAQ advises starting with small batches to test Facebook's limits.
facts: Verified: $8,237 MRR, 337 active subscriptions, $1,796,102 all-time revenue, rank #67 on TrustMRR.
The site claims 120,000+ users. Per TrustMRR, the domain rating is 33/100 and the stack is Rails, Vue.js, PostgreSQL, Redis, DigitalOcean and Stripe.
TrustMRR lists a 100K dormant email list (2019–present) and a Chrome Web Store 'Featured badge' renomination submitted in Q1 2026 as bonus assets and levers.
The Chrome Web Store listing shows version 7.4.4 (extension.vn mirror), while TrustMRR mentions a v7.2.4 maintenance release.
The site states it is not a scraper and runs locally in your browser (support FAQ: it uses your local browser and internet connection).
do_not_claim: Profit or margin (hidden, shown as XX%)
Team size today (the Medium post claims a full-time developer staff, but that is unverified)
Any launch date, Product Hunt launch, or viral moment (none found)
That the $11.3K MRR / ~390 subscribers figures are real (the verified figures are lower)
Sale price or reason for selling (not found)
That the 120,000+ users figure means active users (the Chrome Web Store shows 10,000 users, and the store text says 15,000+ active)
How much revenue comes from affiliates, SEO or the Chrome Web Store (no source)
Exact Rewardful commission rate for FriendFilter beyond the 'up to 50%' on its own page
research.notes: The business is listed for sale, so frame it as 'a Chrome extension business with real Stripe-verified revenue' and not as a founder's current growth story. Use $8,237 MRR and 337 subscriptions, not the listing's $11.3K / ~390. Pricing is consistent across the site and store: $29 and $49 per month, a $9 7-day trial, and Annual $199/year (from the store listing only). The site text offers a '14 day free trial' on some landing pages and a '$9 for 7 days' trial on the homepage, so be careful which one you show. The Medium post is undated but indexed as about 2,400 days old, which fits the March 2019 founding. No founder X posts, interviews, Product Hunt or Indie Hackers pages were found, so the growth section is thin. No third-party source confirmed the Rewardful setup beyond TrustMRR. The 'Best Facebook Friend Remover Extensions' page is the company's own comparison page, so treat its claims as marketing.
